about: The mutant ledger of runtime/v1/rpc: edits of the leaf's source that its own tests must kill. Its rows moved from runtime/v1's ledger when BS8 moved the code into this leaf (re-anchored by wf10 EXPLORE-rt r3). Run it with go run ./scripts/mutants ./runtime/v1/rpc (docs/tooling.md, "Mutant ledger").

mutants.name: rpc-exit-wrapped
mutants.rule: A success's value is written once, into the answer, not first wrapped into an exit text (FD1-g3).

mutants.name: rpc-exits-copied
mutants.rule: The json answer is the Builder's bytes, not copied once more (FD1-g3).

mutants.name: rpc-calls-stop
mutants.rule: A stopped caller's Loopback Call (or a stopped request) ends with the stop, not with a defect read from an Interrupt exit, and after the call's release ran.

mutants.name: rpc-calls-join
mutants.rule: A failed emit (a WriteFailed of the ndjson stream) stops every call of the batch still held and waits for its release before RPCExitLines returns; no call outlives its request. (A stop of the request also reaches each call by the task tree, so TestRPCCallsStopWithTheCaller does not catch this.)

mutants.name: r3b-local-exit
mutants.rule: A Loopback Call reads the json Exit its server answered; the contract's laws hold through it.
killers: examples:limiter (its loopback package: ergo test: limits.Limiter laws for Loopback)

mutants.name: rchk-refused-die
mutants.rule: A Die named RpcError (the server's rpc layer could not read the call) is the typed Transport for a client, not the server's defect (rpc.md, Call).

mutants.name: rpc-wait-unseen
mutants.from: p = rt.Park(t, s, stop, func() bool { return len(s.ended) > 0 })
mutants.rule: A request's wait for its calls is a wait the clock sees: a Loopback call whose handler sleeps on a VirtualClock moves the time and returns (without the park the clock stays still and the call never ends; the test's deadline names it).

mutants.name: rpc-end-unwoken
mutants.rule: A call's end unparks the request's task before the end is visible: under the controlled scheduler a request left parked is never enabled, and the run deadlocks.

mutants.name: rpc-end-hides-stop
mutants.origin: wf10/sync RPC-STOP, moved to the rpc leaf by I22
mutants.rule: A stop wins over a call's end that is ready with it: a stopped request ends with the stop, never with an answer (rpc.md rule 6).

mutants.name: rpc-stop-wait-unparked
mutants.origin: wf10/sync RPC-STOP, moved to the rpc leaf by I22
mutants.from: p = rt.Park(s.t, s, nil, func() bool { return len(s.ended) > 0 })
mutants.rule: A stopped request's wait for its calls left parks, so the explored scheduler and a clock let the calls run to their ends.
